title: Historiography basics
examples: How do different historians view the causes of World War I?
What is the difference between a primary source and a historian's interpretation?
Can one single event be explained by only one cause?

explain.say: Today we will look at how history is written.
Some schools of thought focus on the role of great leaders.
Another view suggests that social structures are the main driver.
Some historians emphasize the importance of culture and ideas.
For example, when studying the Roman Empire, one view might focus on emperors.
In everyday life, think about how a company changes its logo.

faq.a: It is the study of how history has been written over time. It looks at the writing process itself, not just the events.
asks: How do historians write about the past?
What does it mean to study the writing of history?

faq.q: Are all historical accounts equally true?
faq.a: No, because every historian uses different sources and focuses on different causes. This creates different interpretations.
asks: Can one history book be the absolute truth?
Does the historian's viewpoint change the facts?

faq.a: This theory suggests that history is primarily shaped by the actions and genius of a few important people. It focuses heavily on individual biography.
asks: Does history depend on powerful people?
Is it always about the great leaders?

faq.q: How do social structures affect historical writing?
faq.a: Materialist historians argue that economic systems, like class struggle, are the fundamental forces driving historical change. They look at power dynamics.
asks: Is money the most important thing in history?
Do economic factors always cause revolutions?

faq.q: What do cultural historians focus on?
faq.a: They examine how shared ideas, beliefs, and cultural practices shape societies over time. They look at the intangible aspects of life.
asks: Do ideas cause history more than armies?
How important are beliefs in history?

facts: Historiography is the study of historical writing itself.
The Great Man theory emphasizes individual agency in history.
Materialist approaches focus on economic structures and class.
Cultural history examines shared ideas and belief systems.

quiz.say: If a historian focuses only on the decisions made by kings and generals, which school of thought are they most likely following?
quiz.why: This theory directly attributes major historical shifts to the actions of powerful people.

wrong.1: This view prioritizes economic systems over individual actions.
wrong.2: This view focuses on abstract ideas rather than specific leaders.
wrong.3: This is a method of analysis, not a theory of causation.

quiz.say: A study analyzing how trade routes shifted the power of merchant guilds would best fit which historical perspective?
quiz.why: This perspective links changes in economic activity, like trade, to major societal shifts.

wrong.0: This is too narrow; it ignores the broader economic context.
wrong.2: This theory would look for a single person to blame for the guild's success.
wrong.3: This view would focus on the ideas of the guilds, not just their trade.

quiz.say: When examining the Enlightenment, a historian focusing on the rise of reason and scientific thought is using which lens?
quiz.why: This view treats abstract ideas, like reason, as the primary force shaping human societies.

wrong.0: This would look for the underlying economic changes that allowed for the Enlightenment.
wrong.1: This is a tool to check sources, not a theory of causation.
wrong.3: This would single out one philosopher as the sole cause of the Enlightenment.
